decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - The proposed development, by reason of its height, increased massing and close proximity to the shared boundaries with Nos. 914,916 and 918 Garratt Lane, would result in an unacceptable loss of outlook and be an unduly overbearing form of development that would give rise to a sense of enclosure for neighbouring occupiers. As a result, the proposal would cause harm to the residential amenities of neighbouring occupiers, contrary to Policy LP2 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023).

Reason : 2 - The proposed development contains two double bedrooms at basement level, where they would have inadequate levels of daylight and sunlight, poor quality of outlook and an oppressive sense of enclosure. The ground floor bedroom, which would also receive no direct sunlight, would further contribute to the overall provision of substandard internal accommodation. Taken together, these arrangements would lead to unacceptable living conditions for future occupiers, contrary to Policy LP27 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023), Policy D6 of the London Plan (2021) and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

Reason : 3 - The proposed development would fail to provide an adequate amount and quality of private amenity space for future occupiers. The 'walk-on' glazed skylight does not constitute useable external amenity space. The lightwell is below the minimum 15 sqm required, and its confined nature would not provide a practical or pleasant area for everyday outdoor use. The proposal would therefore result in substandard living conditions, contrary to Policy LP27 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023), Policy D6 of the London Plan (2021) and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

Reason : 4 - The proposed development, by reason of its height, bulk, massing and roof form including the introduction of a crown roof and front dormer, would result in a visually dominant and disproportionate building that would fail to respect the established scale and open character of this part of Garratt Terrace. The proposal would erode the low-rise pattern of backland development and would appear incongruous and out of keeping with the immediate surrounding built environment. Consequently, the proposed development would cause harm to the character and appearance of the area, contrary to Policies LP1, LP2 and LP7 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023), Policy D4 of the London Plan (2023) and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

Reason : 5 - Notwithstanding the submitted Energy Statement, insufficient technical evidence has been submitted to demonstrate that the proposed dwelling would achieve a minimum 35% reduction in on-site carbon emissions against the Part L 2021 baseline, including at least a 10% reduction through energy efficiency measures alone. The proposal therefore fails to comply with Policy LP10 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023).

Reason : 6 - In dealing with this application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive manner and the Council has, as far as practicable, sought solutions to problems arising in relation to dealing with the planning application. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies in the Local Plan consisting of the Core Strategy, Development Management Policies Document, Supplementary Planning documents and where appropriate the Site Specific Allocations Document as well as offering a full pre application advice service. However, we have been unable to seek solutions to problems as the principle of the proposal is clearly contrary to our statutory policies and negotiation could not overcome the reasons for refusal.
description: Alterations including erection of two storey 4-bedroom dwelling house with attic and basement floors.
